bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar launches new flood control plan, to use river silt for road construction - India Today
bihar_raw_news.content: SIGN IN Edition IN IN US Download App Follow Us On: News India Bihar launches new flood control plan, to use river silt for road construction Bihar launches new flood control plan, to use river silt for road construction The initiative will involve scientific desilting of rivers, barrages and reservoirs, with the extracted material being reused for infrastructure projects, including National Highway construction. Advertisement Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary during an MoU signing between the state government and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, in New Delhi. (@samrat4bjp/X via PTI Photo) By: Rohit Kumar Singh Patna , Nov 3, 2026 20:19 IST Last Updated Nov 3, 2026 20:19 IST Published by Vivek Nov 3, 2026 20:19 IST Edited by Vivek Kumar The Bihar government has launched the Bihar Water Resources Restoration and Silt Management Policy 2026 to address the long-standing problem of silt accumulation in rivers and reduce flood risks across the state, a statement said. As part of the initiative, silt will be scientifically removed from rivers, barrages and reservoirs and utilised for infrastructure development, including National Highway construction. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the Bihar government have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to facilitate the desilting of water bodies and use suitable extracted material in highway projects. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The agreement was signed in New Delhi in the presence of Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari . The initiative aims to address two key requirements simultaneously: restoring the water-carrying and water-retention capacity of water bodies affected by silt accumulation and ensuring the availability of suitable earth and fill material for highway construction. According to an NHAI statement, the authority has identified a requirement for approximately 243 lakh cubic metres of silt for its ongoing and proposed National Highway projects in Bihar. The state currently has 39 ongoing highway projects covering around 1,561 km, with an estimated cost of Rs 58,340 crore. Additionally, 11 proposed projects covering approximately 1,982 km are expected to involve an investment of Rs 1,85,200 crore. Under the agreement, desilting operations will be undertaken following detailed technical assessments of identified water bodies. The extracted material, subject to quality testing and suitability, will be utilised in National Highway projects in accordance with the applicable Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) specifications and Indian Roads Congress (IRC) codes. The MoU also establishes an institutional framework for coordination between NHAI and the Bihar government. The state's Road Construction Department (RCD) will serve as the nodal agency, while a state-level coordination committee will oversee project proposals, approvals, implementation progress and compliance. The agreement includes safeguards to prevent desilting activities from disturbing ecological balance or damaging riverbanks, embankments, bridges and other structures. Extraction will be allowed only at approved locations and within technically prescribed limits. Bihar is set to develop its first World Athletics Class-1 synthetic track at Pataliputra Sports Complex, Kankarbagh, Patna , by upgrading the existing athletics track to international standards. Key Points Project Implementation: The Sports Department and Bihar State Sports Authority (BSSA) are jointly undertaking the renovation. The objective is to secure World Athletics Class-1 certification by meeting international technical standards . Athletics Track: The existing 400-metre, eight-lane synthetic track will be reconstructed with a full-EPDM (Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer) synthetic surface. Natural Grass Field: The field will be upgraded with improved drainage, irrigation facilities and Bermuda grass. Significance: The upgraded infrastructure will provide international-standard training and competition facilities for Bihar athletes and support the development of athletics in the state. bihar_raw_news.title: Bengaluru to Digitise TDR System for Road Widening Projects - eGov Magazine
bihar_raw_news.content: Home · e-Governance News Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. Photo: Hey Seeta Ram news / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 3.0) Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on 2 November 2026 directed officials to fully digitise Bengaluru’s Transferable Development Rights (TDR) system. Every step, from application and verification to certificate issuance and the later sale and use of TDR certificates, will move to one online platform covering the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA). The minister gave the direction while chairing a meeting with senior officials at Vikasa Soudha in Bengaluru, officials said. The new software is expected to go live in about 10 days. The move adds to the state’s wider push to move citizen services online, after Karnataka ordered all licences and certificates online under Sakala last month. What is the TDR system and why does it matter for Bengaluru? TDR is the compensation that civic agencies offer landowners who give up land for public works such as road widening. Instead of cash, the owner receives a certificate of development rights that can be used for extra construction elsewhere or sold to builders. Krishna Byre Gowda said road widening and new roads are urgent if Bengaluru is to find lasting solutions to its traffic congestion. The city has already turned to technology on the traffic side, with the AI-led ASTraM platform of Bengaluru Traffic Police winning a national award in October. According to the minister, the TDR process has run on paper files for years, with weak tracking and little transparency. He said this had caused public dissatisfaction and loss of confidence in the system, and that procedural delays had reduced the value of TDR as a tool for acquiring land. What the digital TDR platform will cover The minister asked for end-to-end digitisation of the TDR lifecycle. Based on his directions, the platform will handle: Recording of road and property details for each land parcel. Verification and scrutiny at every stage of the process. Online issuance of TDR certificates. Records of the purchase and sale of TDR certificates. Tracking of the final use of each certificate. Property owners and applicants will be able to track the progress of their applications online. The minister said this would end repeated visits to government offices and reliance on middlemen. Why it matters for urban e-governance Land acquisition is often the slowest part of urban infrastructure projects, and paper-based compensation records are hard to audit. A single digital ledger of TDR certificates, from issue to final use, gives the GBA and BDA a clear record of who holds which rights and where they have been used. The step follows a broader shift towards digital land administration across India, from Himachal Pradesh’s land records reforms to Delhi’s plan for property Aadhaar cards under a new land records bill . bihar_raw_news.title: How a Bihar Farmer Built an 18-Acre Aquaculture Enterprise | ICAR
bihar_raw_news.content: The Inspiring Journey of Shri Mithilesh Kumar Singh: From No Pond Ownership to a Crore-Plus Fisheries Enterprise Shri Mithilesh Kumar Singh, a progressive fish farmer from Rohtas district of Bihar, exemplifies the transformative potential of scientific knowledge and institutional support in promoting rural entrepreneurship. From having no prior experience in fisheries and no ponds of his own, he has developed an 18-acre commercial aquaculture enterprise, generating an annual turnover of over ₹1 crore with a net profit margin of 20–25%. His remarkable journey demonstrates how technical training, systematic investment and the adoption of scientific practices can create sustainable livelihood opportunities and strengthen the rural economy. Scientific Training: The Foundation of Entrepreneurial Success Recognising the growing potential of inland fisheries as a viable business opportunity, Shri Singh participated in a seven-day training programme on Inland Fisheries Management organised by ICAR-Central Inland Fisheries Research Institute, Barrackpore, with sponsorship from the Department of Fisheries, Government of Bihar. The programme provided him with practical knowledge and essential technical skills in pond preparation and management, water quality monitoring, fish species selection, stocking density, scientific feeding practices and fish health management. More importantly, the training equipped him with the confidence and technical understanding required to venture into commercial aquaculture. From a Beginner to an 18-Acre Commercial Enterprise Applying the knowledge acquired through the training, Shri Singh gradually established and expanded his fish farming activities through systematic investment, scientific management and sustained entrepreneurial efforts. Today, his enterprise covers approximately 18 acres of pond culture area, including a recent expansion of two acres in 2026. His production system primarily comprises Indian Major Carps (IMC), including Rohu (Labeo rohita), Catla (Gibelion catla) and Mrigal (Cirrhinus mrigala), along with Pangasius (Pangasianodon hypophthalmus). This diversified approach enables efficient utilisation of pond resources while catering to different market requirements. The enterprise currently generates an annual turnover exceeding ₹1 crore, with a net profit margin of 20–25%, highlighting the economic viability and commercial potential of scientifically managed aquaculture. Continuous Learning for Sustainable Growth Recognising that technological advancement and continuous learning are essential for long-term success, Shri Singh returned to ICAR-CIFRI, Barrackpore, in 2026 to participate in an advanced training programme. His continued association with the Institute reflects his commitment to upgrading technical skills, improving production efficiency and adopting improved aquaculture practices to address emerging challenges. Recalling his experience, Shri Singh remarked:“Before coming to ICAR-CIFRI, I knew nothing about fish and fisheries. The scientific training not only enriched my knowledge but also gave me the confidence to build a sustainable commercial business step by step.” Director's Perspective: Empowering Entrepreneurs through Scientific Knowledge The success of Shri Mithilesh Kumar Singh demonstrates how scientific training, technology dissemination and institutional guidance can transform an inexperienced individual into a successful fisheries entrepreneur. ICAR-CIFRI is committed to bridging the gap between scientific knowledge and field-level adoption through farmer-centric capacity building, skill development and the dissemination of appropriate technologies. He pointed out that the Farakka Water Treaty restricts Bihar to receive water for only four months each year. PTI Published On Nov 03, 2026 at 03:48 PM IST Select ETGovernment as Preferred Choice on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Farakka barrage Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday said the state needs adequate water to establish industries and promote economic development, but the current terms of the Farakka Water Treaty with Bangladesh limit Bihar's ability to fully utilise its share of Ganga water. Addressing an event organised by NHAI here, Choudhary said under the Farakka Water Treaty, Bihar has the right to receive water for only four months of a year (July-October) and during these months, it rains in almost every part of the country, and water is readily available. "I am not opposed to Bangladesh receiving its share of water. However, we also need water for agriculture and drinking purposes. Bihar is a poor state, and it needs water to establish industries and promote economic development. We can not compromise on this requirement. It is our necessity," he said. The Farakka Water Treaty (officially called the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty) was signed on December 12, 1996, between India and Bangladesh. The treaty regulates the sharing of the Ganga waters at the Farakka Barrage in West Bengal, primarily during the dry season from January 1 to May 31. The treaty expires in December. "The water-sharing agreement does not give us sufficient opportunities to use the water. It allows us access to water for only four months of the year (July-October). "During these months, as you know, it rains in almost every part of the country, and water is readily available," Choudhary said. The barrage was built in 1975 to divert water from the Ganga into the Hooghly River to flush out silt and to keep Kolkata Port navigable. The 1996 treaty established a 30-year binding framework (1996-2026) to replace earlier short-term stopgap arrangements and ensure predictable water distribution. Seven major rivers in Bihar originate in Nepal and flow into the state "Rivers flowing from Nepal's Terai region cause immense hardship, devastation, and destruction in Bihar; the annual losses amount to ₹10,000 crore," Choudhary said. bihar_raw_news.title: ICAR–MGIFRI, Motihari Organizes Residential Training on Climate-Smart Agriculture and ...
bihar_raw_news.content: 26-29 October 2026, Motihari, Bihar ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar, organized a four-day residential training programme on “Crop Diversification: Benefits and Resilience for Climate-Smart Agriculture” from 26 to 29 October 2026, sponsored by the Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA), Siwan, Government of Bihar. The programme aimed to strengthen farmers' knowledge and practical skills in climate-resilient agriculture, crop diversification, integrated farming systems (IFS), sustainable resource management and income-generating farm enterprises. The training combined expert lectures, practical demonstrations, exposure visits, farmer–scientist interactions and pre- and post-training assessments. Addressing the participants, Dr Raghavendra Singh, Director, ICAR–MGIFRI, emphasized the importance of climate-smart agriculture and diversified farming systems in addressing emerging challenges such as climate variability, declining soil health, rising input costs and increasing production risks. He highlighted that integrating crops with livestock, fisheries, horticulture and other complementary enterprises can enhance resource-use efficiency, provide multiple income opportunities and strengthen the resilience of small and marginal farmers. He encouraged participants to adopt location-specific technologies and disseminate the knowledge gained among fellow farmers. The technical sessions covered key aspects of sustainable agriculture, including soil-health management, balanced fertilization, weather-based agro-advisories, climate-risk management and appropriate crop planning. Discussions also highlighted livestock- and fish-based integrated farming systems, focusing on nutrient recycling, efficient utilization of farm resources, diversified livelihoods and enhanced farm income. Practical demonstrations on integrated farming models, Azolla production, vermicomposting and organic-resource recycling provided hands-on exposure to sustainable and resource-efficient technologies. Participants also visited Kash Krishi Farm and KVK Piprakothi to observe diversified farming practices, mushroom cultivation, nursery management, millet processing and agricultural value-addition technologies. The visits highlighted opportunities for enterprise diversification and income enhancement. The programme also included visits to Kesaria Stupa and the Virat Ramayan Mandir site. The concluding sessions focused on climate-resilient agronomic practices, balanced animal nutrition, locally available feed resources and appropriate agricultural mechanization. Emphasis was placed on integrating classroom learning with practical demonstrations and field exposure to promote technology adoption. Participants were encouraged to apply suitable technologies and adopt an integrated farming approach encompassing crop diversification, soil and water management, livestock, fisheries and value addition to address field-level challenges and enhance farm livelihoods. To assess training effectiveness, pre- and post-training evaluations were conducted among 25 trainees using a structured questionnaire comprising 15 objective and descriptive questions. The assessment covered climate-smart agriculture, crop diversification, soil health, integrated farming systems, flood-resilient agriculture and environmentally sustainable practices. The reported performance ranged from approximately 57% to 78%, providing useful feedback on participants' understanding of the training topics. The programme concluded on 29 October 2026 with a valedictory session, participant feedback and distribution of training certificates. The participants appreciated the combination of scientific lectures, hands-on demonstrations and field exposure, which helped strengthen their understanding of diversified and climate-resilient farming practices. (Source: ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar first state to introduce comprehensive silt management policy : CM Samrat Choudhary
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar first state to introduce comprehensive silt management policy: CM Samrat Choudhary ANI | Updated: Nov 03, 2026 13:32 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 3 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday said Bihar has become the first state in the country to introduce a comprehensive silt management policy, aimed at addressing recurring floods and utilising accumulated river silt for infrastructure development. He made the remarks while addressing an MoU signing programme under the ‘Nadi Sanjeevani’ initiative for river desilting and utilisation of silt in National Highway construction, in the presence of Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and senior officials. Choudhary said the initiative would help Bihar turn its vulnerabilities, particularly floods and silt accumulation, into resources for development. Explaining the state’s flood situation, the Chief Minister said seven major rivers enter Bihar from Nepal, making the state vulnerable to rainfall and water discharge in neighbouring regions. “Bihar has two primary vulnerabilities. The people of Bihar, however, are not devastated by their own water; they are devastated by water originating elsewhere. Seven major rivers enter Bihar from Nepal. Whether it rains in Bihar or not, if it rains in Nepal, Bihar suffers devastation,” he said. Citing this year’s rainfall and river levels, Choudhary said Bihar recorded more than 32 per cent deficient rainfall, but three major rivers still reached peak flood levels. “This year, Bihar recorded more than 32% deficient rainfall. Yet, the High Flood Level (HFL) shifted in three of our major rivers, reaching peak flood levels. And in the Ganga, which functions as our master drain, the 200-year HFL record was broken this time due to the massive volume of water pouring in, whether from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, or the Terai of Nepal,” he said. The Chief Minister referred to changes in the HFL of the Gandak and Sone rivers as well. He said, "The Gandak River, which originates in Nepal and joins at Patna, saw its HFL change. The Sone River, from which we receive water from Madhya Pradesh under the Bansagar agreement, saw its HFL change as well, we received nearly 1.15 million (11.5 lakh) cusecs of water in the Sone." Choudhary said the volume of water released from Nepal, along with the discharge into the Ganga from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, had compounded the problem. “The first time, Nepal released approximately 200,000 cusecs of water, bringing along immense volumes of silt. The second time, they released 550,000 cusecs. Simultaneously, nearly 1.7 million (17 lakh) cusecs of water was discharging into the Ganga collectively from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh,” he said. “Consequently, our master drain was blocked. 550,000 cusecs of water backflowed. And when river flow reverses, our embankments begin to breach,” he added. Highlighting the economic potential of desilting, Choudhary cited the example of Odhni Dam in Banka district. bihar_raw_news.title: Road ministry signs MoU with Bihar to use river silt for national highways construction
bihar_raw_news.content: Representative image. The ministry of road transport and highways and Bihar government will undertake desilting of identified rivers and other water bodies and utilisation of suitable excavated silt in National Highway construction projects in the state. An MoU was signed between the ministry and state of Bihar to this effect on Tuesday. The plan is to use 243 lakh cubic metres of silt in 16 ongoing National Highway projects and another 835 lakh cubic metres for 27 future projects in the state. Currently, 39 projects of the National Highways Authority of India covering approximately 1,561 km, with an estimated investment of Rs 58,340 crore, are under construction in Bihar while another 11 projects covering around 1,982 km and involving an estimated investment of Rs 1,85,200 crore are proposed. The availability of suitable excavated silt is expected to meet a significant part of the material requirement of these projects, reduce construction costs and facilitate timely execution of highway works. Live Events Envisioned as ‘Nadi Sanjivani’, the initiative seeks to restore the water-carrying capacity of rivers and water bodies, strengthen flood management , conserve agricultural land and provide a sustainable source of construction material for National Highway projects. “Accumulated silt has significantly affected the carrying capacity of rivers, contributing to floods, damage to agricultural land and loss of property. Bihar faces recurring challenges of flooding and water scarcity, particularly due to rivers originating in Nepal that carry substantial quantities of water and sediment into the state, road minister Nitin Gadkari said. “Scientific desilting would help improve water flow and drainage, restore water bodies and make suitable excavated material available for highway construction,” he added. Gadkari said that the initiative would create a mutually beneficial framework in which river restoration supports infrastructure development, while utilisation of excavated silt reduces dependence on fresh earth material and agricultural soil. “This would help conserve productive agricultural land, reduce construction costs and facilitate faster completion of highway projects,” he said urging other states facing similar challenges to promote sustainable infrastructure development and improved water management. bihar_raw_news.title: Nikhil Kamath sparks debate on Karnataka's tax revenue, UP and Bihar's share, and China's model
bihar_raw_news.content: Nikhil Kamath sparks debate on Karnataka's tax revenue, UP and Bihar's share, and China's model Nikhil Kamath's comparison of India's tax-sharing model with China's system has triggered a debate online, with users questioning his understanding of how tax revenue is redistributed among states. Moneycontrol News November 03, 2026 / 10:36 IST Nikhil Kamath sparks debate on Karnataka's tax revenue, UP and Bihar's share, and China's model Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath's remarks comparing India's tax-sharing system with China's have triggered a debate on fiscal federalism, with social media users questioning his understanding of how revenue redistribution works. The discussion began after Kamath argued that Indian states do not retain the revenue they generate, unlike their counterparts in China. Citing Karnataka as an example, he suggested that the state's earnings are redistributed to other parts of the country, including Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. What’s wrong with this? @nikhilkamathcio is rightly pointing out the loot of progressive states like Karnataka by the central government (Congress and BJP). https://t.co/tgLyKBtDrk — ಸಂಪತ್ ಕುಮಾರ್ (@SampathKannada) November 2, 2026 "In China, unlike India, if Karnataka is making a certain amount of revenue, it is not spent in states like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. The state gets to keep its credits," Kamath said. He also argued that Chinese provinces have greater freedom to pursue capitalistic economic policies, something he believes Indian states do not enjoy to the same extent. His remarks quickly gained traction on social media, with several users challenging the comparison and arguing that redistribution of resources is an established feature of fiscal federalism across countries. Some also pointed out that revenue redistribution takes place within individual states, including Karnataka. 'That's not how redistribution works': X users push back One user disputed Kamath's comparison with China, arguing that the country also redistributes resources on a significant scale. The user said such arrangements were not unique to India and pointed out that Bengaluru's revenue is also distributed across different parts of Karnataka. Another user appeared to agree with Kamath's broader argument, bringing Maharashtra into the discussion. The user highlighted that Maharashtra contributes more than twice the GST revenue of the second-highest contributing state, Karnataka, but continues to face infrastructure challenges. The user questioned why Maharashtra does not have more extensive metro connectivity, better highways and a stronger pipeline of public infrastructure projects despite its substantial contribution to GST collections. A third user challenged the idea of treating Karnataka's revenue as belonging exclusively to the state. The user argued that administrative boundaries could be redrawn, with Bengaluru potentially becoming a Union Territory or Karnataka being divided into multiple states. Using a hypothetical example, the user questioned whether Bengaluru would then be expected to share its revenue with other regions, including Kalaburagi, if it became a separate Union Territory. bihar_raw_news.title: NBCC Bihar Projects to Deliver 3,331 Homes and Tech Park - NewsIP
bihar_raw_news.content: (03.11.26 – By NewsIP Bureau – Patna) “All without any burden on the State exchequer,” NBCC (India) Limited Chairman and Managing Director Dr. K. P. Mahadevaswamy said of four redevelopment projects planned in Patna under Phase I. The projects are expected to provide 3,331 homes, Bihar’s first Tech Park and modern commercial spaces. Also Read: Business news Four projects planned across Patna NBCC signed memoranda of understanding with departments of the Government of Bihar for the four projects, which cover about 34.34 acres. The signing took place in August, but the source information does not specify the year. Chief Minister Sh. Samrat Choudhary, Deputy Chief Ministers Sh. Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Sh. Bijendra Prasad Yadav, and UDHD Minister Sh. Nitish Mishra were among those present. Also Read: Government and corporate appointments 3,331 homes across income groups Two residential projects will redevelop Bihar State Housing Board sites at Sector 5 (TV Tower) and Sector 6 (Bahadurpur). Together, they are planned to provide 3,331 flats for EWS, LIG, MIG and HIG categories, alongside facilities including shopping areas, clubhouses, gyms, community spaces and offices. Tech Park and commercial development A proposed IT Tech Park for DIT Bihar at Gardanibagh is described as the state’s first. NBCC says it is intended to attract IT companies, startups and investment, while supporting local employment and skills development. The other commercial project is planned at a Water Resources Department site on Bailey Road and includes hotels and commercial spaces. Estimated project value and employment Expected sale and lease proceeds from the four projects are estimated at about ₹5,152 crore, while the tentative project cost is about ₹2,000 crore, excluding GST. The source says the projects require no budgetary assistance from the state government. These are estimates, not reported project outcomes. A NBCC estimates around 40,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities across construction and operational phases. Its breakdown includes construction jobs and related supply-chain work, more than 5,000 direct jobs expected at the Tech Park, and additional jobs in residential, hotel and commercial operations. The figures are projections supplied for the projects. Green construction and next phase NBCC says the developments will incorporate measures such as rooftop solar, LED lighting, rainwater harvesting, wastewater treatment and reuse, and green landscaping. It cites its redevelopment work in New Delhi, including New Moti Bagh, East Kidwai Nagar and Nauroji Nagar, as relevant experience. Proposals for a second phase involving the Building Construction Department, Patna Municipal Corporation and Bihar Urban Infrastructure Development Corporation are at the approval stage, according to the supplied information. NBCC says MoUs with those departments are expected to be signed shortly. Also Read: NBCC to Develop Maharana Pratap Tourist Circuit at Haldighati

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi inaugurates and lays foundation stone Pune Metro projects worth Rs 21,800 crore
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that Pune is playing an important role in shaping the vision of a developed India and that the expansion of the metro network is accelerating the city’s development. The metro has given Pune a new identity by providing citizens with modern, efficient and high-quality public transport facilities, which are also contributing to the city’s economic growth. The Prime Minister extended Diwali greetings to the people before addressing the gathering. The Prime Minister virtually inaugurated the much-awaited Hinjawadi-Maan to Shivajinagar Metro Line 3 by flagging off a metro train. The service will be open to passengers from November 4, 2026. He also virtually performed the foundation stone-laying ceremony for four new Pune Metro Phase-II corridors: Vanaz to Chandani Chowk, Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi, Kharadi to Khadakwasla and Nal Stop to Manik Baug. Governor Jishnu Dev Varma and Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs Manohar Lal attended the programme virtually. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Union Minister of State for Civil Aviation and Cooperation Murlidhar Mohol, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar were present. The Prime Minister said that metro services are now operational in 26 cities across the country, with the total metro network expanding from approximately 248 kilometres to more than 1,200 kilometres. Over one crore passengers travel by metro every day. Maharashtra alone has around 175 kilometres of operational metro network. He further stated that the Central Government has undertaken extensive infrastructure development in the energy, road and railway sectors over the past twelve years to achieve the goal of a developed India. Speaking on the occasion, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said that the Maharashtra Government is committed to expanding the metro network and strengthening public transport facilities through various metro projects. Around 120 kilometres of additional metro corridors will provide citizens with modern, safe and environment-friendly transportation. He added that metro projects would not only reduce travel time but also boost trade, industries, employment opportunities and economic activity. An investment of approximately Rs. 5,000 crore would give a significant boost to the urban economy. He expressed confidence that the metro would become a new engine of urban development. The Hinjawadi-Maan to Shivajinagar Metro Line 3 is 23 kilometres long and has 23 stations. In the first phase, passenger services will begin at 17 stations, while the remaining six stations will be opened in phases by January 2027. The Pune Metro project has received substantial financial investment. More than Rs. 8,300 crore has been spent on Phase I, while approximately Rs. 13,500 crore is expected to be invested in Phase II. The combined expenditure on both phases is estimated to exceed Rs. 22,000 crore. A major feature of Metro Line 3 is that the entire metro service will be operated by women train operators. In addition, 30 per cent of the energy requirement will be met through solar power. The new metro corridor is expected to provide significant relief to IT professionals working at Hinjawadi IT Park, students and daily commuters. It will help reduce traffic congestion, save travel time and strengthen public transportation in Pune. The inauguration marks an important milestone in Pune’s infrastructure development and is expected to give fresh momentum to the city’s economic growth.

national_raw_news.title: Domestic indices surge around 1.6% extending winning streak for fourth consecutive session
national_raw_news.content: Benchmark domestic equity indices surged around 1.6 per cent today, extending their winning streak for the fourth consecutive session. The Sensex jumped 1,225 points to close at 76,918. The Nifty climbed 370 points to settle at 23,811. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained 1.1 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index added 0.3 per cent. I n the Sensex pack, 25 out of 30 constituent companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Hindustan Unilever gained nearly 4.2 per cent, Bharti Airtel jumped four per cent, and HDFC Bank rose over 3.6 per cent. In contrast, PowerGrid dropped almost 2.3 per cent, SBI Bank slipped nearly 1.8 per cent, and NTPC fell almost 0.9 per cent. In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 22 out of 28 sectors ended in the positive zone. Among the top gainers, FMCG surged 3.4 per cent, Realty advanced over 2.3 per cent, and Private Banks rose nearly 2.1 per cent. In contrast, PSU Banks dropped more than 1.3 per cent, Utilities lost almost 0.9 per cent, and Power dipped 0.8 per cent. The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2,510 companies advanced, 1,895 declined, and 201 remained unchanged.

national_raw_news.title: NSE International Exchange extends trading hours to facilitate international investors 53 mins ago 9
national_raw_news.content: The NSE International Exchange (NSEIX), based in Gujarat’s GIFT City, has extended its trading hours to 23:30 hours a day, allowing international investors and trading participants to access markets across Asian, European and American time zones. The NSEIX, in a statement, said that the enhanced market timings came into effect yesterday, with trading operations starting at 3:15 AM India Standard Time (IST) and closing at 2:45 AM IST the following day. The move aims to provide investors with a longer window to trade and greater flexibility to respond to developments in international markets. Under the revised schedule, the morning trading session for NSE IFSC Nifty 50 Index Futures, popularly known as GIFT Nifty, now begins at 5:15 am IST instead of 6:30 am. GIFT Nifty is closely tracked by investors and traders as an indicator of the likely opening trend of the benchmark Nifty index. NSEIX said the initiative would strengthen GIFT City’s role as an international financial centre connecting India with global capital markets. The extended trading window is also expected to help participants manage their market exposure across different global time zones. It added that with this initiative, NSEIX has set a new global benchmark to provide a continuous market for nearly 24 hours a day, five days a week. NSEIX is an international multi-asset exchange set up on June 5, 2017. It is recognised by the International Financial Services Centres Authority. The exchange offers a range of financial products, including Indian single-stock derivatives, index derivatives, currency derivatives, depository receipts and global stocks. NSE International Exchange has said that it will continue to focus on expanding international market access and developing market infrastructure to meet the changing requirements of global participants.

national_raw_news.title: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu makes landfall near Ongole, Andhra Pradesh 9 hours ago 304
national_raw_news.content: Cyclone Murasu over the West Central Bay of Bengal crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narasapur, close to Ongole, early this morning with wind speed of 100-110 kilometres per hour, gusting to 120 kilometres per hour. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said that it lay centered over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh. It is likely to continue to move North-northwestwards and weaken gradually into a cyclonic storm by noon and further into a deep depression by midnight of today. The IMD has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Andhra Pradesh and Telangana today. According to IMD, places over Chhattisgarh, Odisha, South Interior Karnataka, Coastal Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal will experience heavy rainfall today. The Met Department has forecast thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds over Konkan, Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha for the day. Meanwhile, the air quality in Delhi-NCR continues to remain in the very poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s air quality index was recorded at 331 at 7 AM. The sub-committee of the Commission for Air Quality Management has imposed Graded Response Action Plan- GRAP-2 restrictions in the National Capital Region. An Air Quality Index between 0 and 50 is considered good, 51 and 100 satisfactory, 101 and 200 moderate, 201 and 300 poor, and 301 and 400 very poor. An AQI between 401 and 500 is considered severe.

national_raw_news.title: Pm Narendra Modi to inaugurate and lay foundation stone of Pune Metro projects today Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of Pune Metro projects worth around 21,800 crore rupees today through video conferencing. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The Prime Minister will inaugurate Pune Metro Line 3, also known as the Pink Line, built at a cost of over 8,300 crore rupees. The project represents an important step towards strengthening Pune's urban mobility infrastructure through technological innovation and modern transportati...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of Pune Metro projects worth around 21,800 crore rupees today through video conferencing. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The Prime Minister will inaugurate Pune Metro Line 3, also known as the Pink Line, built at a cost of over 8,300 crore rupees. The project represents an important step towards strengthening Pune’s urban mobility infrastructure through technological innovation and modern transportation solutions. Spanning approximately 23 kilometres, the Pink Line connects Maan to District Court Metro station. The corridor will provide Metro connectivity between the Hinjewadi IT hub and Shivajinagar, improving access to one of Pune’s major employment centres and facilitating the daily commute of thousands of IT professionals and other commuters. The corridor will integrate with the existing metro network, providing seamless connectivity across different parts of Pune. It will help reduce dependence on private vehicles, ease traffic congestion and vehicular emissions, and improve access to major commercial and residential areas. A notable feature of the Pink Line is its emphasis on women’s empowerment and gender-inclusive public transportation. The line will be operated entirely by women train operators, making it a first-of-its-kind initiative. The project also emphasises environmental sustainability, with approximately 30 per cent of its total electricity requirements envisaged to be met through solar power. Mr Modi will also lay the foundation stone of Phase-II of Pune Metro, to be developed at an estimated cost of around 13,500 crore rupees. Phase-II comprises Pune Metro Lines 2A, 2B, 4 and 4A, which will substantially expand the city’s Metro network and strengthen connectivity across important residential, commercial and IT hubs. Under Phase-II, Lines 2A and 2B will span a total length of around 12.75 kilometres. Line 2A will connect Vanaz to Chandani Chowk, while Line 2B will connect Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi, extending the existing east-west Metro network. Line 4, spanning around 25.52 kilometres, will connect Kharadi to Khadakwasla. Line 4A, spanning 6.12 kilometres, will connect Nal Stop to Manik Baug. The new Metro corridors will connect several important locations, including Kharadi, Magarpatta, Hadapsar, Swargate, Manik Baug, Nanded City, Pune Cantonment and Warje. The eastern extension from Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi will improve connectivity to rapidly developing residential, commercial and IT hubs in Kharadi and Wagholi. The corridors will integrate with intercity bus services and the existing Pune Metro network through interchange facilities at Swargate, Nal Stop and Kharadi Bypass, facilitating seamless connectivity across different parts of the city. These projects will strengthen Pune’s public transportation infrastructure, improve connectivity across the city and provide commuters with an efficient and integrated urban mobility network.

national_raw_news.title: Unbeaten India register fifth successive win in Asian Champions Trophy Punjab 2026, set up semi-final clash against Korea
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Men’s Hockey Team completed an unbeaten league-stage run at the Hero Asian Champions Trophy Punjab 2026 on Monday with an 8-0 win over Korea – their fifth in a row – at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar. Dilpreet Singh (8′, 40′) scored twice, while Jugraj Singh (11′), Harmanpreet Singh (15′), Shilanand Lakra (33′), Sukhjeet Singh (34′), Sanjay (36′) and Angad Bir Singh (60′) were also on target. India finished at the top of the standings with five wins from five matches and will face Korea again in the semi-finals as the tournament moves to Mohali, where the semis will be played on November 4 and the medal matches on November 5. Second-placed Japan will face Malaysia, who finished the league stage in third place, in the other semi-final. India began aggressively in front of a packed house and created an early chance through Sukhjeet, whose backhand effort in the fourth minute was saved by goalkeeper Kim Jaehyeon. Dilpreet opened the scoring in the eighth minute with a backhand finish after a move that began with an aerial pass from Jugraj. India doubled their lead through a penalty corner in the 11th minute, with Jugraj scoring after Harmanpreet’s initial effort was kept out and Vishnukant Singh set up Jugraj on the rebound. Harmanpreet added another penalty-corner goal to his tally in the 15th minute to give India a 3-0 lead at the first break. He now tops the scoring chart with nine goals. Korea showed more intent in the second quarter and earned a number of penalty corners, but the Indian defence kept them at bay. Pathak also denied Son Dain in a one-on-one situation in the 27th minute with a timely save using his outstretched foot. India had opportunities of their own, but Aditya Arjun Lalage’s shot went wide, while another penalty corner did not result in a goal after the ball was ruled to have been played with the back of the stick. India went into half-time with their three-goal advantage intact. India increased the tempo after the break and added four goals in the third quarter. Shilanand Lakra scored in the 33rd minute after a penalty-corner variation. Harmanpreet’s pass found Jugraj, whose attempt was saved by Kim, but Lakra was on hand to put away the rebound. Sukhjeet made it 5-0 a minute later, deflecting Aditya’s pass from the baseline into the net. Sanjay added another in the 36th minute, reacting quickest after Dilpreet’s attempt was saved. India’s seventh goal came in the 40th minute when Sanjay controlled Harmanpreet’s long aerial pass and struck towards goal, with Dilpreet getting a touch to send the ball past the goalkeeper. India eased the tempo in the final quarter, with Korea enjoying periods of ball-possession but struggling to create clear chances. Suraj Karkera made a save when Korea threatened, while a penalty corner in the 58th minute came to nothing. Angad Bir Singh then scored a superb solo goal in the 60th minute, winning possession in the midfield, driving towards the circle and pushing the ball underneath the advancing goalkeeper to complete the 8-0 win. Korea had another penalty corner in the closing seconds, but failed to make the most of it. Sanjay, who was named ‘Player of the Match’, said India were pleased to finish at the top of the pool. “We wanted to top the table and we did that. We are very happy. I want to request the crowd to support us the same way in Mohali,” he said. India finished with 15 points and a goal difference of +29. Japan ended second with 10 points, followed by Malaysia with nine and Korea with six points. -IANS

national_raw_news.title: “Huge honour for India,” says Rijiju as Bhutan dedicates Stupa 76 to PM Modi
national_raw_news.content: Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Sunday expressed gratitude towards Bhutan after the King of Bhutan dedicated Stupa number 76 to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Rijiju represented India at the ceremony for raising and consecrating 108 Stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City. In an X post, he wrote, “It’s a huge honour for India that very sacred stupa 76 is dedicated to Hon’ble PM @narendramodi ji for his outstanding vision and commitment to friendship between India and Bhutan. On the auspicious occasion of Lhabab Duchen, joined the sacred ceremony in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan, marking the raising and consecration of 108 stupas, accompanied by the blowing of Dungchens.” “Paid my respects and offered prayers in the presence of His Majesty the King of Bhutan, Her Majesty the Gyaltsuen, H.E. Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Prime Minister of Bhutan & the people of Bhutan. A deeply meaningful spiritual occasion, reflecting Bhutan’s rich Buddhist heritage and the enduring bonds of friendship between our two nations,” he added. According to the Ministry of Minority Affairs, Rijiju conveyed gratitude on behalf of Prime Minister Modi to the King of Bhutan for the gesture of dedicating a Stupa as part of the Project. The 108 Stupas project was conceived by the King of Bhutan, who also steered its implementation. In a single day, thousands of volunteers erected 108 Stupas, each 15 metres tall and separated by 108 metres on an 11.7 kilometre stretch along the Aie (Mau) River within Gelephu Mindfulness City near the border with Assam. The project aims to showcase Gelephu Mindfulness City as a prominent centre of Vajrayana Buddhism, while simultaneously representing the values and culture of the Bhutanese people, the ministry stated. Earlier today, Rijiju called on Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay in Gelephu, where the two leaders held “warm and very positive” discussions aimed at strengthening the India-Bhutan partnership and exploring the potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City project. “Delighted to call on H.E. Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Hon’ble Prime Minister of Bhutan, in Gelephu today. Had a warm and very positive discussion on India-Bhutan partnership, and the immense potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City for both nations. India remains a steadfast partner in Bhutan’s path of growth and prosperity,” Rijiju posted on X. The Union Minister is on a visit to Bhutan from October 31 to November 2. The two sides have maintained a healthy trend in bilateral cooperation in diverse areas including development cooperation, trade, energy, investment, connectivity and cultural connections. -(ANI)

national_raw_news.title: India committed to protecting integrity of sports: Mansukh Mandaviya at 10th WAADS QA ...
national_raw_news.content: India committed to protecting integrity of sports: Mansukh Mandaviya at 10th WAADS QA Managers’ Meeting 2026 Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर India committed to protecting integrity of sports: Mansukh Mandaviya at 10th WAADS QA Managers’ Meeting 2026 ANI | Updated: Nov 03, 2026 19:49 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 3 (ANI): Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya, on Tuesday, launched the Extramural Research Grant Policy of the National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL) at the 10th World Association of Anti-Doping Scientists (WAADS) Quality Assurance Managers’ Meeting 2026 in New Delhi, according to a press release from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. The two-day meeting that began on November 2 was organised by NDTL and brought together international stakeholders from the sports and scientific communities. Mandaviya, as the chief guest, also oversaw the launch of the NDTL Newsletter at the meet. The Union Sports Minister Outlined India’s zero tolerance policy for doping. He said, “Friends, India has zero tolerance for doping. Our responsibility is to ensure that every victory is earned through talent, discipline, and hard work. Over the last two years, under the leadership of our Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, sports has been recognised as an important pillar of nation-building,” said Dr. Mandaviya. “India’s sporting journey has entered a new phase.” Highlighting India’s commitment towards further anti-doping research and education, the Union Minister said, “Today we launched the important Extramural Research Grant Policy, which aims at promoting research and development in areas of advanced detection and prevention. This initiative will strengthen the scientific foundation of our anti-doping efforts.” With India set to host Commonwealth Games 2030 and harbouring ambitions of hosting the 2036 Olympics, education and awareness about doping play a vital role in India’s fight towards preventing it. Mandaviya said, “Our approach, therefore, combines stronger testing infrastructure with education, awareness, and prevention. As India prepares to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030 and with our dreams of hosting the 2036 Olympics as well, anti-doping testing, athlete education, and international cooperation are a priority for us.” “Athletes, coaches, and medical professionals must understand the implications of prohibited substances, the risks associated with supplements, and their responsibilities under anti-doping rules,” Mandaviya added. The Union Sports Minister stated that India has already taken major steps towards becoming a sporting nation, and the recent performances of its athletes at the 2026 Asian Games prove that. “Through initiatives such as Khelo India, which translates to Play India, Fit India, and the target Olympic podium scheme, we have strengthened the sporting ecosystem and created greater opportunities for our youth to excel,” said Mandaviya. “At the recently concluded Asian Games 2026, our athletes delivered one of their best performances, finishing fourth in the final medal tally. Our para-athletes have also scripted history at the Asian Para Games 2026, securing a record 114 medals, our highest ever medal tally at the games,” he said. Over the two days, the meeting was also attended by Secretary (Sports)...
